findings.evidence: "This field takes a maximum of 30 characters. Shorten the entry and save again."
findings.fix: Name the field explicitly in the message text, e.g. "Postal code takes a maximum of 30 characters."
findings.location: Checkout form, shipping address - first entry, Message line
findings.violation: The message says "This field" instead of naming the field (e.g., "Postal code"), so it has no meaning on its own and relies entirely on visual proximity - a problem for screen-reader users or anyone who loses that positional context.

findings.evidence: "Predictable mistake: yes" paired with "Suggested fix: none"
findings.fix: Suggest a proactive fix, such as a live character counter or truncation as the user types, instead of "none."
findings.location: Checkout form, shipping address - first entry, Predictable mistake / Suggested fix rows
findings.violation: A 30-character maximum is fully foreseeable and preventable (e.g., via a live character counter or input truncation), yet no proactive fix is suggested despite the mistake being flagged as predictable.

findings.evidence: "Placement: directly below the shipping address block" / "Signal: bold text set above the address block at a larger size than its labels, icon"
findings.fix: Make Placement and Signal agree on a single position for the message.
findings.location: Checkout form, shipping address - second entry, Placement vs. Signal rows
findings.violation: Placement and Signal directly contradict each other about where the message appears relative to the address block (below vs. above).

findings.evidence: "Please correct the highlighted field. Error code: 502."
findings.fix: Replace with a specific, user-actionable description of the problem, and move the technical error code (if needed for support) out of the primary message or into fine print.
findings.location: Checkout form, shipping address - second entry, Message line
findings.violation: The message is vague (doesn't say what's wrong) and exposes a raw HTTP-style error code to the end user; 502 is a gateway/server error, not something a shopper can act on by "correcting a field."

findings.fix: Reclassify this as a system/server error rather than a predictable mistake, and handle it with retry logic rather than field-correction guidance.
findings.location: Checkout form, shipping address - second entry, Predictable mistake row
findings.violation: A 502-style error indicates a server/infrastructure failure, not a predictable user input mistake, so classifying it as a "predictable mistake" is inconsistent with the message content.

findings.evidence: "Fires: on-blur" with a message reading "Error code: 502"
findings.fix: Change the trigger to on-submit (or whenever the failing request actually occurs) rather than on-blur.
findings.location: Checkout form, shipping address - second entry, Fires row
findings.violation: A gateway/server error would surface from a submission request, not from a field losing focus, so the firing trigger doesn't match the nature of the error.

findings.evidence: "described, names the one available alternative but requires the reader to enter it by hand" vs. "selectable, offers a convert and retry action in place of the message"
findings.fix: Offer an equivalent automated action for the size error (e.g., a "compress and retry" option) instead of requiring manual resizing.
findings.location: File upload, receipts - first entry vs. second entry, Suggested fix rows
findings.violation: Both errors are marked "Predictable mistake: yes," but only the format error gets an automated one-click remedy; the size-limit error leaves the user to manually figure out how to shrink the file.

findings.fix: Validate file format immediately upon selection (after-field-complete), matching the size-limit check's timing.
findings.location: File upload, receipts - first entry vs. second entry, Fires rows
findings.violation: Two validations on the same upload control fire at different times, so a wrong-format file isn't flagged until final submission while an oversized file is flagged immediately - an inconsistent and needlessly late check for format.

findings.evidence: "Choose a password of at least 8 characters, long enough that a guessing attack cannot work through every combination."
findings.fix: Remove or correct the justification; state the requirement plainly without an inaccurate security guarantee.
findings.location: Password reset, new password - first entry, Message line
findings.violation: This is a misleading security claim - an 8-character minimum alone does not make exhaustive guessing infeasible, especially without complexity requirements or rate limiting.

findings.evidence: "at the top of a long form, requiring the reader to scroll up to see it, though the field itself stays visible on the page"
findings.fix: Move the message to appear directly adjacent to the password field instead of at the top of the form.
findings.location: Password reset, new password - first entry, Placement row
findings.violation: The error is displaced far from the field it describes, forcing unnecessary scrolling even though the field itself is on screen - a proximity violation.

findings.evidence: "Container: toast" vs. "Placement: in a dialog centered on the password reset step, over the new password field it blocks" / "Signal: bold heading text at the top of the dialog, icon"
findings.fix: Relabel the container as "dialog" (or "modal") to match the described behavior.
findings.location: Password reset, new password - second entry, Container vs. Placement/Signal rows
findings.violation: "Toast" denotes a transient, non-blocking notification, but the description is of a centered, blocking modal dialog - the container type contradicts its own placement and signal description.

findings.evidence: "Fires: on-focus" for message "This reset link expired an hour after it was sent"
findings.fix: Fire this message immediately on page load/mount rather than on-focus.
findings.location: Password reset, new password - second entry, Fires row
findings.violation: Link expiration is known as soon as the page loads, but waiting for the user to focus the field delays telling them, allowing interaction with a dead page in the meantime.

findings.evidence: "Predictable mistake: yes" with message "The last changes were not saved and cannot be recovered. Contact support for assistance."
findings.fix: Reclassify this as a system error rather than a predictable mistake.
findings.location: Account settings, username - entry, Predictable mistake row
findings.violation: An unrecoverable save failure requiring support intervention is a system failure, not a predictable user mistake, so the classification doesn't match the described event.

findings.evidence: "Signal: bold text set larger than the field label, icon" for an unrecoverable, irreversible data-loss message, vs. a full blocking dialog used for the recoverable expired-link case
findings.fix: Escalate the signal for unrecoverable data loss (e.g., a blocking dialog) so visual weight matches severity.
findings.location: Account settings, username - entry, Signal row compared to Password reset second entry
findings.violation: The visual severity signal is inverted relative to actual severity - an irreversible loss gets a minor inline treatment while a recoverable issue gets a blocking modal.

findings.evidence: "Input on resubmission: preserved" next to message "cannot be recovered"
findings.fix: Clarify what is preserved (e.g., the currently-typed value only, not the lost prior save) or remove the field if nothing meaningful is preserved.
findings.location: Account settings, username - entry, Input on resubmission row
findings.violation: It's unclear what "preserved" refers to when the message states the prior changes cannot be recovered - the field is contradictory or at least unexplained given the stated data loss.

findings.evidence: "Fires: on-blur" for message "The last changes were not saved and cannot be recovered."
findings.fix: Surface this message immediately when the save failure occurs, not on a subsequent on-blur event.
findings.location: Account settings, username - entry, Fires row
findings.violation: An unrecoverable save failure is reported only when the user later blurs the field again, deferring notice of a past, already-occurred data loss instead of surfacing it at the moment it happened.
